prize_parts.citation: for formalising how special-interest politics shapes trade policy, and for their analysis of the interplay between trade, innovation and growth

statement.case_for: My configuration is unchanged: a single part, B001, crediting Grossman and Helpman. My confidence is lower than in round 1, because the exchange made the B001-versus-B020 choice closer than my opening suggested. The case rests on three things. First, the protection-for-sale framework answers a first-order question, why governments depart from free trade, with a tractable equilibrium model that makes political influence an explicit and estimable object. The trade-innovation-growth models add a second, separate strand on how openness interacts with endogenous growth. Second, attribution is the cleanest on the shortlist, a sustained two-person partnership. That matters more to me now, since the exchange showed that the main weakness of the leading rival, B020, is an unresolved credit boundary that cannot be repaired within the credited list. Third, the work is three decades old and has been extended, taught and tested, so there is no maturity concern. On the chair's weighting question, I would apply one common test to all four leading candidates. It asks how important the question is, how durable and cleanly attributable the contribution is, and how much it changed what other researchers could do, whether through theory or through measurement. Direct empirical confirmation counts most where a contribution is presented as a finding about the world. It counts less where the contribution is a framework that made a question answerable. B001 is mainly the second kind, and I say so openly in the citation. On impact outside trade theory and political economy, my recollection is that the lobbying and influence-bidding formulation has been carried into the study of other regulated or subsidised policy areas, and that the trade-and-growth models inform open-economy growth analysis. I have not verified this, and I treat it as supporting evidence of modest weight. The case rests mainly on the framework's influence within its own area. If the Committee prefers B020, I could accept it as a single-part award and regard it as my clear second choice.
statement.case_against: The empirical record for the protection-for-sale predictions is mixed. Several colleagues, including Friberg, Strömberg and Enflo, treat that as a real reason to rank B001 below B020, and I accept that it is the main weakness of my first choice. B020's footprint in firm-level data, estimation and quantitative policy evaluation is plainly wider. A prize is also about what the field can now do, and on that criterion B020 may be stronger. A second concern is the unverified question of how much of B001's novelty lies in the application and tractable estimable form, since the common-agency and menu-auction machinery it uses came from earlier work. A third concern is that Helpman is credited on both B001 and B020, so recognising him through B001 is a choice about which strand to honour. That framing choice could crowd out the candidate with the stronger empirical record. B016 has the broadest programme, but I still hold the 2024 overlap and the identification weakness against it.

responses.point: Friberg ranks B020 first and B001 eighth. He argues that the selection and reallocation mechanisms have been checked against firm-level data in many countries, while protection for sale has been confirmed less consistently. He says he could accept B001 if the Committee prefers it, but that B020 is stronger on empirical confirmation.
responses.response: This is the strongest argument against my position, and I accept its factual core. B020 has the wider empirical footprint and B001's test record is mixed. Our difference is what a prize should reward when the two properties come apart. I weigh a framework that made a long-standing question tractable and estimable, and I treat mixed estimates as the ordinary fate of a testable model. You weigh confirmation more. I do not read your eighth place as a judgement that the contribution is minor. What keeps me on B001 is attribution. A Helpman-Melitz award would have to be worded around a credit boundary you and others call real but unresolved. On your point that Helpman should not be stacked across both strands, I agree, and I do not propose it.

responses.point: Enflo ranks B020 first and says cleaner credit does not make a contribution larger. She sees B001 as a close alternative, and would word a B020 citation around the mechanism and not around priority.
responses.response: I agree that cleaner credit does not make a contribution larger, and I do not use it that way. I use it as a tiebreaker between two contributions that I regard as comparably large. Your suggestion of mechanism-centred wording for B020 is sensible and makes the award more defensible. It would not close the gap, because a citation can avoid claiming priority but cannot add names outside the credited list. If the Committee judges that gap tolerable, I would not resist B020. I also note that I am a Lund colleague of yours, as your own disclosure records. That does not affect this reading, but I flag it.

responses.point: Hassler ranks B016 first and B001 as his first alternative. He weighs the breadth of a research programme above a single framework. He does not treat B001's mixed empirical record as disqualifying, and he asks that B020 be tested directly against B001.
responses.response: I accept your account of the difference between the 2024 prize and B016, rules and fiscal outcomes versus historical origins, and I now see the overlap as a smaller risk than I treated it in round 1. It does not remove my other reasons. The credit between the Persson-Tabellini and Besley-Persson strands cannot be cleanly separated, and the identification of constitutional effects is weaker than in the other leading candidates. Breadth of programme is a real merit, and on that count B016 beats B001. I place it behind because I weigh attribution and testability above breadth. I agree that the B001-versus-B020 choice should be argued on the merits of each contribution and not decided by treating Helpman as a bridge between them.

responses.point: Teorell ranks B001 first and wants the case to stand on protection for sale and the trade-innovation-growth models, not on Helpman's credit elsewhere. He puts B020 behind mainly because of its attribution gap, and says the mixed empirical support should be stated openly.
responses.response: I agree on both points, and I have tightened my case accordingly. I do not rely on Helpman's B020 work to strengthen B001. The citation I propose refers only to the political-economy and trade-innovation-growth contributions, and it states that the influence is on the framework. I part from you slightly on B016. You treated its identification problems as decisive against it, but I think breadth and cumulative field-building count for it, and that is why it is still my second alternative. I note that your support for B001 and mine are not fully independent. We reach it by similar reasoning about attribution, so the Committee should not count our agreement as extra evidence.

responses.point: Hjalmarsson ranks B001 first and asks the Committee to separate contested magnitudes from no lasting contribution. She says she would move toward B020 before moving to another field if B001's mixed empirical support is found decisive.
responses.response: I agree with your distinction and rely on it. I also agree with your ordering of fallbacks: if the Committee finds the empirical record decisive, B020 is the right substitute and B016 is the next. I would add one qualification to the point about mixed results. A framework earns credit for making a question estimable only if later work has used it that way, and I believe it has, though I have not verified the extent. The Committee should check this in the scientific background before relying on the argument, and not accept it because two of us find it persuasive.

uncertainties: Whether the Committee judges the B020 credit gap (Bernard, Eaton, Jensen, Kortum) disqualifying. If it does not, B020 is a strong rival to B001 and I would not oppose it.

How far mixed empirical support for protection-for-sale should weigh against its influence as a framework. Members who rank B020 first and members who rank B001 first apply different weights, and I have not found a neutral way to settle it.

How much of the novelty in the protection-for-sale framework lies in the application and estimable form, given the earlier common-agency and menu-auction machinery. This is from my recollection and I have not verified it.
Whether the evidence of B001's impact outside trade theory and political economy is as broad as I believe. I have not verified it.
Whether field balance, given the 2008 trade prize, should count at all. I do not treat it as merit, and it applies equally to B001 and B020.

I have not independently verified citations or priority claims. My assessment rests on my recollection and on colleagues' written positions, which in part reflect shared reasoning and are not independent evidence.
statement.conflict_note: No tie to any credited candidate on B001, B020 or B016 is apparent from my supplied profile. It lists no co-authorship or institutional link to Grossman, Helpman, Melitz, Persson, Tabellini or Besley. My profile records me as an SSE affiliate alongside committee colleagues Dreber Almenberg, Friberg and Strömberg. Enflo's round-1 file and the chair summary also record a Lund tie between us. These are collegial ties among committee members, not links to a candidate. My own research in mechanism design and social choice is thematically adjacent to the mechanism-style reading I give B001. I disclose this adjacency without adjudicating it. My 2020 presentation speech was delivered for the Academy and does not indicate a preference among current candidates.
